title: The Frank Tapes
description: Just Ronnie and Frank, one on one, after midnight. No Barry to keep them honest. Generated with Dia.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: It's just you and me tonight, Frank. Barry went home. Said he needed to, quote, be around normal people.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Normal people are the most dangerous kind, Ronnie. That's exactly who they recruit.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, that's why I keep you on the line. You connect the dots the rest of us are too scared to look at.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: I don't sleep anymore, Ronnie. Sleep is when they update you.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Update you. Like a phone.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Exactly like a phone. Why do you think you wake up tired? A real rest would leave you sharp. They don't want you sharp.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I did wake up tired this morning. I thought it was the coffee.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: The coffee is part of it, but that's a different tape. We'll get to the coffee.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Okay. Okay, walk me through tonight's, then. What did you bring me?

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Escalators, Ronnie. (laughs) Nobody questions the escalators.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I ride one almost every day. At the mall.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: And where does the staircase go, Ronnie, when it folds under at the bottom? Where does it go?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I always assumed it just... loops around. Underneath.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: That's what the diagram says. But have you seen the diagram? Or did they just tell you about the diagram?

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I have never once seen the diagram. (laughs) I just assumed somebody had.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Nobody has, Ronnie. The steps go down, and they keep going. All the way down. To the warehouse.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: The warehouse. The same warehouse from the pigeon tapes?

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: It's all one warehouse, Ronnie. It always was. The pigeons, the bread, the escalators. One roof.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That is... honestly, that's almost comforting. At least it's organized.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Oh, they're very organized. That's the scariest part. (sighs) You don't run an operation like this without a calendar.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Frank, can I ask you something, just between us? Doesn't it ever get heavy? Knowing all this?

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Every single day, Ronnie. But somebody has to stay awake. Somebody has to refuse the update.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Well. You've always got a friend on this frequency. You know that.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: I know, Ronnie. And when they come for the radio towers, you'll be the first one I call.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: I'd be honored, Frank. Don't feed the pigeons. Don't trust the escalators.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: And take the stairs, Ronnie. The regular ones. The ones that don't move.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: We'll be right back, after this. Stay awake out there.
